patient.name: Marcus Webb
patient.chiefComplaint: Partial amputation of right hand, industrial accident

history.hpi: Right hand caught in a metal stamping press at work. Coworkers immediately shut down and locked out the machine and freed the hand, which is partially amputated at the wrist with a narrow skin bridge intact. A coworker trained in first aid applied a leather belt as an improvised tourniquet proximal to the wrist before EMS arrival and retrieved the amputated portion.
history.lastOralIntake: Coffee and a sandwich approximately 3 hours prior to the incident
history.events: Right hand caught in a stamping press during a shift; coworkers shut down the machine, freed the hand, applied an improvised belt tourniquet, and called 911.

scene.dispatch: 47-year-old male, industrial accident, arm injury, manufacturing facility
scene.location: Metal stamping floor of a manufacturing plant; patient seated on the floor against machinery with coworkers nearby
scene.safety: Machine powered down and locked out by the shift supervisor prior to EMS arrival; floor otherwise clear of hazards
scene.bystanders: Shift supervisor and a coworker present; the coworker applied an improvised belt tourniquet and retrieved the amputated portion
visualCues: Right hand partially amputated at the wrist with a narrow skin bridge intact
Leather belt cinched proximal to the wrist as an improvised tourniquet
Amputated portion wrapped in a shop rag nearby
Blood-soaked rags and pooling on the floor near the patient
Patient pale, diaphoretic, guarding the injured arm

phases.name: Initial Contact
phases.description: Crew arrives to find a 47-year-old male seated on the floor, alert and in severe distress, with his right hand partially amputated at the wrist. An improvised belt tourniquet is in place proximal to the injury, applied by a coworker before EMS arrival.

clinicalPresentation.breathing: Nonlabored but rapid, 22/min, symmetric chest rise
clinicalPresentation.circulation: Radial pulse present and rapid on left; belt tourniquet in place on right wrist with slow ongoing oozing beneath it
clinicalPresentation.motorFunction: Strength intact in left arm and both legs; right hand non-assessable distal to injury
otherFindings: Right hand partially amputated at the wrist with a narrow skin bridge
Improvised leather belt tourniquet in place, not fully occlusive
Amputated portion wrapped in a shop rag at scene
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: "My hand — it's still bleeding, please help me, it hurts so bad."

transitions.condition: Crew assesses the improvised tourniquet, upgrades to a commercial tourniquet, and provides weight-based ketamine analgesia.

phases.name: Hemorrhage control and analgesia initiated
phases.description: Crew reassesses the improvised belt tourniquet, replaces it with a properly applied commercial tourniquet, marks the time of placement, administers weight-based ketamine for pain, and packages the amputated part for transport.
phases.triggerCondition: After confirming no other life threats on primary survey, the crew recognizes the improvised tourniquet is not fully occlusive and proceeds to upgrade hemorrhage control while addressing severe pain.

clinicalPresentation.circulation: Radial pulse present bilaterally, commercial tourniquet in place with bleeding stopped and distal pulse eliminated
clinicalPresentation.motorFunction: Strength intact in left arm and both legs
otherFindings: Commercial tourniquet applied 2-3 inches proximal to the wound, time marked
Amputated portion wrapped in saline-moistened gauze, bagged, and placed on ice in a second bag
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: "That's a lot better, thank you — it doesn't hurt as bad now."

expectedActions.shortAction: Reassess improvised belt tourniquet; apply commercial tourniquet 2-3 in proximal to wound until bleeding stops
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: If improvised tourniquet has been placed by bystander, reassess, and consider placing commercial tourniquet proximal to it. Tourniquet should be placed 2–3 inches proximal to wound, not over a joint, and tightened until bleeding stops and distal pulse is eliminated
expectedActions.rationale: The improvised belt tourniquet is not confirmed fully occlusive; a properly applied commercial tourniquet ensures definitive hemorrhage control.

expectedActions.shortAction: Mark tourniquet placement time on the patient and in the patient care report
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Mark the time of tourniquet placement prominently on the patient and in the patient care report
expectedActions.rationale: Tourniquet time is critical information for receiving trauma teams regarding limb ischemia time.

expectedActions.shortAction: Ketamine 22.5 mg IV (90 kg x 0.25 mg/kg = 22.5 mg; max initial 25 mg, max cumulative 100 mg)
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Ketamine: 0.25 mg/kg IM, IV or IO (maximum initial dose 25 mg; maximum cumulative dose 100 mg)
expectedActions.rationale: Severe traumatic pain warrants weight-based opioid-class analgesia per protocol dosing.

expectedActions.shortAction: Wrap amputated hand in saline-moistened gauze, seal in a bag, then place that bag on ice in a second bag
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Amputated body parts should be transported with patient for possible re-implantation. It should remain cool but dry. Place the amputated part in a plastic bag. Place the bag with the amputated part on ice in a second bag. Do not let the amputated part come into direct contact with the ice
expectedActions.rationale: Proper cooling without direct ice contact preserves tissue viability for possible re-implantation.

transitions.condition: Commercial tourniquet is confirmed occlusive with bleeding stopped, ketamine has reduced the patient's pain, and the amputated part is packaged for transport.
The crew delays upgrading the improvised tourniquet, and the improvised belt continues to allow slow ongoing blood loss.

phases.name: Tourniquet secured and ketamine given
phases.description: Bleeding is controlled with a properly applied and time-marked commercial tourniquet, pain is well managed with ketamine, and the patient is packaged for prompt transport with the amputated part.
phases.triggerCondition: After definitive tourniquet placement and ketamine administration, the patient's pain and hemodynamics improve and the crew prepares for transport.

clinicalPresentation.circulation: Radial pulse present bilaterally, tourniquet holding, no active bleeding
clinicalPresentation.motorFunction: Strength intact in left arm and both legs
otherFindings: Amputated part packaged appropriately and accompanying patient
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: "I feel a lot calmer now. Is my hand going to be okay?"

expectedActions.shortAction: Reassess tourniquet and pain level en route without loosening the tourniquet
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Without removing the tourniquet or dressing, reassess frequently for signs of ongoing or renewed bleeding, such as: Blood soaking through dressing; Bleeding distal to tourniquet
expectedActions.rationale: Ongoing reassessment confirms the tourniquet remains effective without disturbing hemorrhage control.

phases.name: Tourniquet delayed
phases.description: The improvised belt tourniquet is left in place without reassessment or upgrade. Ongoing slow blood loss continues, and the patient begins to show early signs of hemorrhagic shock.
phases.triggerCondition: The crew focuses on analgesia or other tasks without promptly reassessing and upgrading the improvised tourniquet, allowing continued blood loss.

clinicalPresentation.circulation: Radial pulse weak and rapid, improvised tourniquet with visible ongoing oozing
clinicalPresentation.motorFunction: Strength intact in left arm and both legs
otherFindings: Belt tourniquet visibly loosening with continued blood loss
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: "I feel really dizzy and cold... is it still bleeding?"

expectedActions.shortAction: Apply commercial tourniquet immediately; hemorrhagic shock developing from delayed hemorrhage control
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Survival is markedly improved when a tourniquet is placed *before* shock develops
expectedActions.rationale: Continued delay in definitive tourniquet placement is allowing progression toward hemorrhagic shock.
